title: Blob Containers, Objects, and Metadata
description: Learn how blob containers organize blobs, how to work with blob metadata and tags, and how to manage blob versions.

data.text: Blob containers are more than simple folders. They define the security boundary for your blobs and support metadata, tags, immutability policies, and versioning. Understanding these features helps you build maintainable, searchable storage solutions.

When you create a container, you choose a public access level. This controls whether anonymous users can read blobs inside the container. You can also keep the container fully private and use tokens for controlled access.

data.title: Access Levels
items: **Private (no public access)** — only authenticated requests with proper keys or tokens can access blobs.
**Blob (anonymous read access for blobs only)** — anyone with the blob URL can read the blob, but cannot list containers.
**Container (anonymous read access for container and blobs)** — anyone can list and read blobs. Use only for truly public content.

data.text: Blobs support **metadata** — name-value pairs stored with the blob that describe it. For example, you might store an upload date, a project ID, or an author. Metadata is returned with blob properties and is useful for filtering or organizing content.

data.title: Set Blob Metadata with Azure CLI
data.content: Add metadata to an existing blob
data.code:
az storage blob metadata update \
  --account-name stdemostorage \
  --container-name uploads \
  --name photo.jpg \
  --metadata project=website uploadedby=admin date=2025-01-15

data.text: Blob versioning keeps previous versions of a blob when it is overwritten or deleted. Combined with **soft delete**, this protects you from accidental data loss. If a user overwrites or deletes a blob, you can restore an earlier version.

rows: Retains deleted data for a configurable retention period
Prevents changes for a fixed time or until a legal hold is released

terms.definition: Name-value pairs stored with a blob for indexing, filtering, or organizational purposes.
Indexed key-value pairs on blobs that can be used for fast filtering and lifecycle management.
A retention policy that preserves deleted or overwritten blobs for a set period so they can be recovered.
Automatic tracking of previous blob versions when data is overwritten or deleted.

data.title: Cost of Versioning
data.text: Versioning and soft delete use extra storage. Always set a retention period and consider cost when enabling these features on high-throughput containers.

data.title: Exercise: Manage Blob Metadata
data.description: Upload a file, add metadata, and inspect it from the Azure Portal.
steps: Upload a text file named notes.txt to your container.
Use the Azure CLI to add metadata: category=draft, author=yourname.
Open the blob in the Azure Portal and verify the metadata values.
Upload a new version of notes.txt and observe the version history if versioning is enabled.
data.expectedOutcome: A blob with metadata and an observable version history if versioning is enabled.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Container public access levels control who can read your blobs.
Blob metadata and tags help you organize and filter data.
Versioning and soft delete protect against accidental data loss.
These features add storage cost, so plan retention carefully.
data.takeaway: Containers, metadata, and versioning turn raw blob storage into a manageable, safe data platform.
